paragraphs.text: In today's headlines on work and AI, business-standard.com reports that HSBC reorganizes support roles in India, impacting hundreds of jobs. economictimes.indiatimes.com carries a headline attributing to JP Morgan the claim that 24 million jobs are at risk globally over the next five years due to AI. phoronix.com (via Hacker News) reports that SUSE is laying off 10% of its workforce due to AI and automation.

sources.title: HSBC reorganizes support roles in India, impacting hundreds of jobs
JP Morgan: 24 million jobs at risk globally over the next five years due to AI
SUSE Laying Off 10% of Its Workforce Due to AI and Automation

paragraphs.text: Other headlines offer commentary. jsdev.space (via Hacker News) and gadgetreview.com (via Hacker News) both say AI layoffs are backfiring as companies rehire workers. zerohedge.com asks who pays for a $2 trillion deficit if AI takes jobs. braidwoodtimes.com.au reports that ASIS is recruiting in Canberra with jobs paying up to $210,000.

sources.title: AI Layoffs Backfire as Companies Start Rehiring Workers
The AI Layoff Experiment Is Backfiring as Companies Rehire Humans
Robo-cession: If AI Takes The Jobs, Who Pays For The $2 Trillion Deficit?
ASIS recruits in Canberra with jobs paying up to $210,000

paragraphs.text: On earthquakes, the USGS recorded an M6.8 earthquake 105 km NE of Lospalos, Timor Leste, an M6.5 earthquake in the Vanuatu region, and an M6.4 earthquake in the Mauritius - Reunion region. The USGS also listed an M5.9 earthquake 238 km SW of Yanglong, China, and an M4.2 earthquake 10 km WSW of Point MacKenzie, Alaska.
